corrections.why: The archive gives 'Year Discontinued: 1961' and the county says the light was taken out of service in 1961; the OSM-derived 'active' status is wrong.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources disagree on whether the light is still lit. The archive and the county both date its discontinuance to 1961, and the county says it was taken out of service then; it is an inactive historic light, lit only as a restored exhibit if at all.

The archive records cast iron on a stone pier with a cast-iron caisson; the county and Visit Sleepy Hollow describe a concrete-and-metal caisson, and the county and Visit Sleepy Hollow also call the structure a conical steel structure. Not resolved; the story gives both descriptions.

The 1891-92 Board text about 'the new light' concerns a recommended light on the Oyster Beds shoal off Rockland Lake Landing (printed p. 60), not the Tarrytown light. The story no longer identifies that light as Tarrytown; Kingsland Point Light appears in the text as the turning mark.

notes_for_editor: Corrected 2026-10-22: the 1891-92 river-directions passage (scan 79, printed p. 60, checked on the page image) concerns a recommended light on the Oyster Beds shoal off Rockland Lake Landing, not the Tarrytown light; the earlier draft misread it. Printed page numbers now checked on page images: scan 79 = p. 60 (1891-92), scan 313 = p. 10 (1893-94), scan 81 = p. 64 (1893), scan 66 = p. 59 (1896; the earlier 'p. 56' was wrong; item 355 is on that page, not scan 67). Scan 380 printed page not confirmed. Bulletin: the Brown commendation is in the 1 July 1925 issue (printed p. 85 per the 1924-29 index, PDF p. 27); the entry gives only '8 June', so the year is taken from the issue, not stated in the source text. Thin early history: the NRHP nomination is not digitized (placeholder, 22 KB); the Board reports for 1883-1890 are not in the corpus; no newspaper hit for the 1883 lighting. Wikipedia (lead only, not cited) gives a 1894 color change (the Board report says 30 Sept 1893), a 1902 flashing change, a 1957 cut to 1,500 cp, the Moreland family and a 1974-75 county purchase; left out. Wikipedia says Jacob Ackerman was a schooner captain who saved 19 lives, citing a 1997 book not read; left out. Keeper count: County 14, Visit Sleepy Hollow eight families, roster 13 keepers plus one USCG name. Position: USLHS gives 41 deg 05.03 N, 73 deg 52.29 W (to the minute); not proposed as a correction. Wikimedia Commons photo in the record not checked for license. Verification: 2026-10-22 fact-check; keeper stints used from the USLHS roster page; no roster line was matched by OCR column position.
